human_claim: For every number field K and every smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve C over K of genus greater than one, the set C(K) of K-rational points is finite.

quantifier_scope.object: a smooth, projective, geometrically connected curve C over K
quantifier_scope.hypothesis: the geometric genus of C is greater than one
quantifier_scope.conclusion: the set of K-rational points C(K) is finite

degenerate_cases: Genus zero and genus one are excluded; finiteness is not true in this generality there.
Geometric connectedness and geometric integrality conventions must be reconciled rather than silently interchanged.
The rational-point set may be encoded as sections or slice morphisms only after a checked equivalence.
The theorem is not broadened to arbitrary finitely generated fields or higher-dimensional varieties.
foundation_profile: classical, nonconstructive algebraic geometry and number theory are expected; the exact axiom closure is unaudited
tcb_profile: Lean 4 kernel, pinned mathlib closure, toolchain, and any later pinned external dependency; not frozen at intake
